A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CARINOX study. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and the equations, tables, figures, and relocated material support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation experiments, a 200-prompt human evaluation, and supplementary GenEval, MS-COCO, and resource measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds adaptive-weighting, gradient-norm, regularization, and matched-generator-evaluation analyses.

M1.justification: The default reward set, uniform weights, clipping, regularization, and exploration procedure remain unchanged. Appendix F introduces an optional ablation variant that replaces uniform weights with category-specific correlation weights selected using ground-truth category labels.

E1.justification: Both versions use T2I-CompBench++, HRS, GenEval, and MS-COCO with the same task coverage. The added experiments examine configurations and components within existing coverage.

E2.justification: The new ablations introduce CARINO (AW) and a version without regularization as comparison variants against the corresponding full methods. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark tables is unchanged; newly discussed SMC and flow methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix I.2 adds a fixed budget of 50 generator evaluations, including CARINOX with two seeds and 25 iterations, alongside the retained five-seed, 50-iteration configuration. The weighting ablation uses ground-truth categories and weights summing to four; the regularization ablation specifies that other settings are held fixed. Existing experimental protocols are retained.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands checks of the design: Appendix E quantifies gradient imbalance, Appendix F tests adaptive versus uniform weighting, Appendix I.2 examines performance under matched generator-evaluation budgets, and Appendix J isolates regularization. These supplement the retained reward-component, iteration/seed, and qualitative clipping analyses.

E5.justification: New Table 8 reports means and standard deviations of per-reward gradient norms across prompts/seeds at selected iterations. This adds statistical reporting for the diagnostic analysis; it does not establish increased repeated runs or add uncertainty estimates to the retained benchmark scores.

E6.justification: All ten original tables retain their numerical results after matching renumbering. Substantial new findings include persistent gradient-scale imbalance, marginal adaptive-weighting effects, degradation without regularization, and CARINOX means of 0.5531, 0.5531, and 0.5522 for the new two-seed/25-iteration setting in Table 12. These are additional results under new controls, not improvements over v1 under unchanged conditions.

T1.justification: Appendix F adds Equation 15 defining normalized category-specific correlation weights, with their sum fixed at four. The existing optimization, regularization, and diffusion mathematics remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions and performance claims: combining exploration with optimization, selecting complementary rewards through human correlation, and improving alignment while preserving quality and diversity.

C2.justification: v2 interprets adaptive weighting as offering limited additional benefit and explains clipping through persistent scale differences and occasional extreme gradients. Appendix I expands the explanation of computational overhead and interprets the matched-generator-evaluation results as evidence that gains do not require a larger generator-call budget.

D1.justification: Appendix I newly identifies an NVIDIA H100 for resource measurements. v2 also documents the adaptive-weight calculation and category-label requirement and corrects Algorithm 1's parameter list to include the regularizer and consistent regularization-strength notation. The project-page link is unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work expands to DAS, flow-model inference scaling, Psi-Sampler, DOODL, D-Flow, and ORIGEN. Section 4.2 also adds the authors' earlier evaluator-study citation. Several duplicate references are consolidated and citations corrected, while the overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 adds a latent-search related-work subsection, reorganizes baseline descriptions and the resource appendix, inserts new ablation sections, and adds publication and review information.

P2.justification: v2 adds three supporting tables and a regularization figure, reformats figure labels, and relocates existing displays. Table 4's incorrect iteration/seed caption is replaced with a reward-component caption. Existing qualitative examples and sensitivity plots are preserved.

improvement.justification: The new component ablations, gradient statistics, and matched-generator-evaluation comparison strengthen support for the existing design, while hardware disclosure and the corrected Table 4 caption improve clarity. The gain is limited: primary results remain unchanged, and matching generator calls does not equalize reward-model costs or runtime, so the new compute-fairness interpretation remains only partly supported.
